message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"2.21","text":"These men met Zacchaeus while he was staying here and, through him, shared in the word of truth. Having regretted their initial innovations, they quickly condemned Simon. Since they had been privy with him to everything, as soon as I arrived here they came to me together with the woman who had raised them. They were introduced to me by Zacchaeus, and from then on they have always remained with me, benefiting from the teachings of the truth. After Peter said this, he sent for them and ordered them to set out for me in detail everything concerning Simon. They called God as witness that they would tell no lie, and began their account.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τοῖς πρώτοις νεωτερισμοῖς μεταμεληθέντες","chosen":"Having regretted their initial innovations","rationale":"μεταμέλομαι here expresses regret over their earlier novel or disruptive activities, not necessarily the fuller moral-spiritual redirection covered by the reorientation terminology policy."},{"source_quote":"πάντα αὐτῷ συνειδότες","chosen":"Since they had been privy with him to everything","rationale":"σύνοιδα with a dative can describe shared inside knowledge. The dative most naturally refers to Simon, though “knowing everything about him” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ τῆς ἀναθρεψαμένης αὐτοὺς","chosen":"together with the woman who had raised them","rationale":"The feminine article and participle identify a woman, while the verb denotes bringing up or rearing."},{"source_quote":"ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ συσταθέντες μοι","chosen":"They were introduced to me by Zacchaeus","rationale":"Zacchaeus is the contextually suitable antecedent of αὐτοῦ; συνίστημι here means to present or introduce people to someone."},{"source_quote":"τῶν τῆς ἀληθείας ἀπολαύοντες μαθημάτων","chosen":"benefiting from the teachings of the truth","rationale":"ἀπολαύω can mean enjoy, partake of, or receive benefit from; the context concerns continuing instruction."},{"source_quote":"τὸν θεὸν μαρτυράμενοι μηδὲν ψεύσασθαι","chosen":"They called God as witness that they would tell no lie","rationale":"The construction invokes God as witness to the truthfulness of the account about to be given."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ συσταθέντες μοι","issue":"The masculine singular pronoun is grammatically capable of referring to more than one previously mentioned man. Zacchaeus is chosen because he is present locally and serves as the source of their instruction, whereas referral by Simon after they had condemned him is contextually unlikely.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.22","text":"Of these, Aquila was the first and began to speak as follows: “Listen, dearest brother, so that you may know precisely everything concerning the man—whose son he is, who he is and where he comes from, what he does, and how and why. This Simon’s father is Antonius and his mother Rachel. He is a Samaritan by nationality, from Geththon, a village six schoeni from the city. Having spent time in Alexandria near Egypt, he thoroughly trained himself in Greek learning, became very powerful in magic, and grew conceited. He wants to be regarded as some supreme power, higher even than the God who created the world. At times, while also hinting that he himself is the Messiah, he calls himself ‘the Standing One.’ He uses this designation on the ground that he will always stand and has no cause of decay that would make his body fall. Nor does he say that the God who created the world is supreme. He does not believe that the dead will be raised. He repudiates Jerusalem and advances Mount Gerizim in opposition to it. In place of our actual Messiah, he proclaims himself. He allegorizes the provisions of the Law according to his own preconception. He says that there will be a judgment, but he does not expect it; for if he were convinced that he would be judged by God, he would not have dared to act impiously even against God himself. Consequently, some people, not knowing that he uses reverence for God as a veil and stealthily plunders what belongs to the truth, believe as trustworthy the hope and judgment that he says will somehow come to pass, and they perish.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τίνος τε ὢν καὶ τίς καὶ πόθεν","chosen":"whose son he is, who he is and where he comes from","rationale":"τίνος ὢν concerns parentage or family origin here, as confirmed by the immediately following identification of Simon’s parents."},{"source_quote":"σαμαρεὺς τὸ ἔθνος","chosen":"a Samaritan by nationality","rationale":"τὸ ἔθνος identifies Simon’s ethnic or national affiliation."},{"source_quote":"ἀπὸ Γετθῶν κώμης","chosen":"from Geththon, a village","rationale":"Geththon is a source-transparent representation of Γετθῶν; forms such as Gitta or Gittha are also used for the place name."},{"source_quote":"σχοίνους ἕξ","chosen":"six schoeni","rationale":"The schoenus was an ancient unit whose length varied; retaining the unit avoids imposing an unsupported modern conversion."},{"source_quote":"ἐν Ἀλεξανδρείᾳ τῇ πρὸς Αἴγυπτον γεγονώς","chosen":"Having spent time in Alexandria near Egypt","rationale":"γεγονώς indicates Simon’s presence or residence there in this context. The phrase may alternatively be understood as “having been in Alexandria in Egypt.”"},{"source_quote":"ἀνωτάτη τις εἶναι δύναμις καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ τὸν κόσμον κτίσαντος θεοῦ","chosen":"some supreme power, higher even than the God who created the world","rationale":"The genitive associated with the superlative presents Simon’s claimed power as surpassing even the creator God."},{"source_quote":"χριστὸν ἑαυτὸν αἰνισσόμενος","chosen":"hinting that he himself is the Messiah","rationale":"αἰνίσσομαι denotes suggesting indirectly or obscurely; χριστός functions here as the independent title “Messiah.”"},{"source_quote":"ἑστῶτα προσαγορεύει","chosen":"he calls himself ‘the Standing One’","rationale":"The perfect participle is used as a substantive designation and initiates the repeated standing-and-falling imagery."},{"source_quote":"αἰτίαν φθορᾶς, ὥστε τὸ σῶμα πεσεῖν , οὐκ ἔχων","chosen":"has no cause of decay that would make his body fall","rationale":"The result clause explains the bodily implication Simon associates with his designation."},{"source_quote":"τὸ Γαριζεὶν ὄρος ἀντεισφέρει","chosen":"advances Mount Gerizim in opposition to it","rationale":"ἀντεισφέρω means to bring forward as a counterclaim or substitute; Jerusalem supplies the contextual object of the opposition."},{"source_quote":"ἀντὶ τοῦ ὄντος χριστοῦ ἡμῶν","chosen":"In place of our actual Messiah","rationale":"ὁ ὤν contrasts the real or actual Messiah with Simon’s self-proclamation."},{"source_quote":"τὰ δὲ τοῦ νόμου ἰδίᾳ προλήψει ἀλληγορεῖ","chosen":"He allegorizes the provisions of the Law according to his own preconception","rationale":"πρόληψις denotes a prior assumption or preconceived notion that controls his allegorical treatment."},{"source_quote":"μέχρι αὐτοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀσεβεῖν","chosen":"to act impiously even against God himself","rationale":"μέχρι marks the extreme extent of Simon’s impiety, reaching even to God."},{"source_quote":"προκαλύμματι τῇ θεοσεβείᾳ κεχρημένος","chosen":"he uses reverence for God as a veil","rationale":"θεοσέβεια is presented as a covering or façade rather than as genuine devotion."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ὁπώσποτε ὑπὸ αὐτοῦ ἐλπίδα καὶ κρίσιν λεγομένην ἔσεσθαι, ὡς πιστῶς πιστεύοντες","chosen":"believe as trustworthy the hope and judgment that he says will somehow come to pass","rationale":"The rendering takes the accusative phrase as the object of πιστεύοντες, ὑπὸ αὐτοῦ with λεγομένην, and ὁπώσποτε with the promised occurrence."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὴν ὁπώσποτε ὑπὸ αὐτοῦ ἐλπίδα καὶ κρίσιν λεγομένην ἔσεσθαι, ὡς πιστῶς πιστεύοντες ἀπόλλυνται","issue":"The syntax is compressed. ὁπώσποτε may qualify either what Simon says or how the hope and judgment are supposed to come about, while πιστῶς may describe the manner of believing or present Simon’s claim as trustworthy. The main rendering treats the hope and judgment as the object of belief and retains the indefinite force of ὁπώσποτε.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.23","text":"The way he slipped into the doctrine of reverence for God came about as follows: There was a certain John, a daily baptizer, who, according to the principle of pairing, also became the forerunner of our Lord Jesus. Just as our Lord had twelve apostles, bearing the number of the sun’s twelve months, so John too had thirty men as chief disciples, fulfilling the moon’s monthly reckoning. Within that number there was one woman named Helena, so that not even this might lie outside the ordered scheme. For the woman, being half a man, made the count of the thirty incomplete, just as the moon’s count is incomplete, since the moon’s journey does not complete its course in a month. Among these thirty, Simon held first place under John and was the most highly approved. The reason he did not assume leadership after John’s death was this:","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸ παρεισελθεῖν αὐτὸν τὸν τῆς θεοσεβείας λόγον","chosen":"The way he slipped into the doctrine of reverence for God","rationale":"παρεισέρχομαι suggests entering surreptitiously or intrusively, while λόγος here denotes a body of teaching or doctrine."},{"source_quote":"ἡμεροβαπτιστής","chosen":"a daily baptizer","rationale":"The compound describes one who practices daily baptism; “Hemerobaptist” is a possible technical transliteration."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὸν τῆς συζυγίας λόγον","chosen":"according to the principle of pairing","rationale":"συζυγία denotes a pairing or paired correspondence, a structural principle in the work’s argument."},{"source_quote":"ἐγένετο πρόοδος","chosen":"became the forerunner","rationale":"πρόοδος concerns going forth or going before and here identifies John’s precursor role."},{"source_quote":"τῶν τοῦ ἡλίου δώδεκα μηνῶν φέροντες τὸν ἀριθμόν","chosen":"bearing the number of the sun’s twelve months","rationale":"The source explicitly correlates the twelve apostles with the twelve solar months."},{"source_quote":"ἕξαρχοι ἄνδρες γεγόνασιν τριάκοντα","chosen":"had thirty men as chief disciples","rationale":"ἔξαρχοι denotes leading or chief persons. “Disciples” is supplied from their subsequent description as fellow disciples, while “men” preserves ἄνδρες."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα μηδὲ τοῦτο ἀνοικονόμητον ᾖ","chosen":"so that not even this might lie outside the ordered scheme","rationale":"ἀνοικονόμητος means unarranged or outside an ordering plan; the clause treats Helena’s inclusion as part of the numerical scheme."},{"source_quote":"ἥμισυ γὰρ ἀνδρὸς οὖσα ἡ γυνὴ","chosen":"For the woman, being half a man","rationale":"The source’s gendered numerical claim is translated directly without endorsement or mitigation."},{"source_quote":"ἀτελῆ τὸν τῆς τριακοντάδος τέθεικεν ἀριθμόν","chosen":"made the count of the thirty incomplete","rationale":"Within the author’s calculation, Helena is counted as half, producing a correspondence with the incomplete lunar month."},{"source_quote":"τούτων δὲ τῶν τριάκοντα τῷ Ἰωάννῃ πρῶτος καὶ δοκιμώτατος ἦν ὁ Σίμων","chosen":"Among these thirty, Simon held first place under John and was the most highly approved","rationale":"The dative associates the group and Simon’s standing with John; δοκιμώτατος can mean most approved, esteemed, or tested."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ μὴ ἄρξαι αὐτὸν","chosen":"he did not assume leadership","rationale":"ἄρχω here concerns taking the leading position after John rather than merely beginning an action."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἕξαρχοι ἄνδρες γεγόνασιν τριάκοντα, τὸν μηνιαῖον τῆς σελήνης ἀποπληροῦντες λόγον. ἐν ᾧ ἀριθμῷ μία τις ἦν γυνὴ λεγομένη Ἑλένη","issue":"The source first calls the thirty ἄνδρες, “men,” and then states that one member of the number was a woman. The following explanation deliberately develops this numerical tension, so no correction is proposed.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.24","text":"For while Simon was away in Egypt to advance his training in magic, John was killed. A certain Dositheus, who coveted the leadership, falsely announced Simon’s death and succeeded to the sect. Simon returned not long afterward and, though he laid strong claim to the position as his own, when he met Dositheus he did not demand it back, knowing that the person who first secures the leadership is not deposed against his will. Therefore, under a pretense of friendship, he submitted himself for a little while to second place under Dositheus. After not many days, once he had been ranked among the thirty fellow disciples, he began secretly to disparage Dositheus, alleging that he was not transmitting the teachings authentically. He said that Dositheus did this not out of envy but out of ignorance. At one point Dositheus perceived that Simon’s artful disparagement was undoing the estimation in which the majority held him, so that he was no longer thought to be the Standing One. He came in anger to their customary session and, finding Simon, struck him with a staff; but the staff seemed to pass through Simon’s body as through smoke. Astonished at this, Dositheus said to him, “If you are the Standing One, then I worship you.” When Simon said, “I am,” Dositheus recognized that he himself was not the Standing One, fell down, and worshiped him. He lowered himself alongside the twenty-nine chief disciples and installed Simon in the place of esteem that had been his own. And so, after not many days, while Simon stood, Dositheus himself fell and died.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τὴν τῆς μαγείας ἐπάσκησιν","chosen":"to advance his training in magic","rationale":"ἐπάσκησις denotes continued practice, training, or cultivation of an ability."},{"source_quote":"θάνατον αὐτοῦ ψευδῆ καταγγείλας","chosen":"falsely announced Simon’s death","rationale":"The pronoun most naturally refers to the absent Simon, whose supposed death would remove his claim to succeed John."},{"source_quote":"διαδέχεται τὴν αἵρεσιν","chosen":"succeeded to the sect","rationale":"διαδέχομαι denotes taking over in succession; αἵρεσις here is the organized school or sect formerly led by John."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ τόπου ὡς ἰδίου μεγάλως ἀντεχόμενος","chosen":"though he laid strong claim to the position as his own","rationale":"τόπος denotes the leadership position, and ἀντέχομαι expresses holding firmly to or asserting a claim."},{"source_quote":"ὁ φθάσας τῆς ἀρχῆς παρὰ προαίρεσιν οὐ καθαιρεῖται","chosen":"the person who first secures the leadership is not deposed against his will","rationale":"φθάνω marks priority in obtaining the office; παρὰ προαίρεσιν is understood as removal contrary to the officeholder’s choice."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ προσποιητοῦ φιλίας","chosen":"under a pretense of friendship","rationale":"The expression conveys assumed or feigned friendship rather than genuine affection."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὸν δεύτερον τοῦ Δοσιθέου τόπον δίδωσιν ἑαυτόν","chosen":"he submitted himself for a little while to second place under Dositheus","rationale":"The phrase places Simon in the subordinate, second-ranking position relative to Dositheus."},{"source_quote":"ταγεὶς δὲ μετ’ οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας τοῖς τριάκοντα συμμαθηταῖς","chosen":"After not many days, once he had been ranked among the thirty fellow disciples","rationale":"The dative can mark the group to which Simon was assigned or attached. The alternative “appointed over the thirty” is possible but less consistent with his stated second-place status."},{"source_quote":"ὑποδιαβάλλειν ἤρξατο τὸν Δοσίθεον","chosen":"he began secretly to disparage Dositheus","rationale":"The compound denotes covert or insinuating slander rather than an open accusation."},{"source_quote":"ὡς μὴ παραδιδόντα γνησίως τὰ μαθήματα","chosen":"alleging that he was not transmitting the teachings authentically","rationale":"γνησίως can mean genuinely, faithfully, or authentically; Simon’s accusation concerns the quality of Dositheus’s transmission."},{"source_quote":"λύουσαν αὐτοῦ τὴν πρὸς τοὺς πολλοὺς ὑπόνοιαν","chosen":"was undoing the estimation in which the majority held him","rationale":"ὑπόνοια here is taken as the opinion or estimation attached to Dositheus among the wider group, not as Dositheus’s own suspicion."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τὴν συνήθη παραγενόμενος διατριβὴν","chosen":"He came in anger to their customary session","rationale":"διατριβή can denote a place or session of teaching and association; the context depicts the group’s regular gathering. The phrase “in anger” represents the preceding θυμῷ."},{"source_quote":"ἡ δὲ ὥσπερ καπνοῦ τοῦ Σίμωνος διελθεῖν ἔδοξε σῶμα","chosen":"but the staff seemed to pass through Simon’s body as through smoke","rationale":"The feminine pronoun ἡ refers back to ῥάβδῳ, the staff, while καπνοῦ supplies the comparison."},{"source_quote":"Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ ἑστώς, καὶ προσκυνῶ σε","chosen":"If you are the Standing One, then I worship you","rationale":"καί is taken with apodotic force, introducing Dositheus’s response to the condition; “I too worship you” is also grammatically possible."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς εἰκοσιεννέα ἑξάρχοις συγκαταβαλὼν ἑαυτὸν","chosen":"He lowered himself alongside the twenty-nine chief disciples","rationale":"συγκαταβάλλω depicts Dositheus lowering himself into their rank after surrendering the leadership."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ τῆς ὑπονοίας τόπον ἔστησε τὸν Σίμωνα","chosen":"installed Simon in the place of esteem that had been his own","rationale":"The phrase identifies Dositheus’s former position as one grounded in the group’s estimation of him; ἔστησε also continues the standing imagery."},{"source_quote":"ἐκείνου στάντος, αὐτὸς πεσὼν ἐτελεύτησεν","chosen":"while Simon stood, Dositheus himself fell and died","rationale":"The literal standing-and-falling contrast is preserved because it concludes the wordplay surrounding the designation “the Standing One.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ταγεὶς δὲ μετ’ οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας τοῖς τριάκοντα συμμαθηταῖς","issue":"The dative with ταγείς permits more than one relation: Simon may be assigned among or to the thirty fellow disciples, or possibly appointed in authority over them. The main rendering chooses membership or ranking among them because the preceding sentence places him second under Dositheus.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τὴν τοῦ Σίμωνος ἔντεχνον διαβολὴν λύουσαν αὐτοῦ τὴν πρὸς τοὺς πολλοὺς ὑπόνοιαν, τοῦ μὴ αὐτὸν εἶναι νομίζειν τὸν ἑστῶτα","issue":"The attachment of the genitive infinitive is compressed. It can express the result of Simon’s disparagement—that Dositheus was not thought to be the Standing One—or characterize the opinion being dissolved. The result construction is adopted because it fits both λύουσαν and the ensuing attack.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ τοῖς εἰκοσιεννέα ἑξάρχοις συγκαταβαλὼν ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ τῆς ὑπονοίας τόπον ἔστησε τὸν Σίμωνα","issue":"The expression τὸν ἑαυτοῦ τῆς ὑπονοίας τόπον is unusual and may denote Dositheus’s place in public estimation, his supposed status, or the position he believed himself to hold. The main rendering chooses public esteem because the preceding sentence concerns how the majority regarded him.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
